Name: PVR:  Preventing PVR Initiation of Same Rx Number+NCPDP With Other Flows (S.07)
Acceptance Criteria: Before a PVR case is initiated, PARP will do a check against the other flows and remove any claims from a PVR case that have the same Rx number at the same NCPDP ID that is present in the OA/DA correspondence table.If the PVR case has more than 1 claim, only the claim that has an Rx number+NCPDPID duplicated with another flow will be removed.  The remaining claim(s) will continue to be included in the PVR case initiation.If the PVR case has only 1 claim and the claim has an Rx number+NCPDPID that is duplicated with another flow, the case will be resolved-cancelled and a PVR initial letter will not be sent. Given before PVR case is initiatedWhen PARP will cross-check the claim(s) in the PVR case to see if any claim has the same Rx number from the same NCPDP ID as a claim that is in the OA/DA correspondence table and the OA/DA is in a status other than Resolved-FAFR Submitted or Resolved-CancelledThen PARP will remove the claim(s) with the duplicated Rx number(s) from the PVR case Given a PVR case has more than 1 claimWhen one or more claim(s) has/have an Rx number+NCPDPID duplicated with another flow in OA/DA correspondence table and the OA/DA is in a status  other than Resolved-FAFR Submitted or Resolved-CancelledThen the duplicated claim(s) will be removed from the case and any remaining claims will continue to be included in the PVR during case initiation Given a PVR case has only 1 claimWhen the claim has an Rx number+NCPDPID duplicated with another flow in OA/DA correspondence table and the OA/DA is in a status other than Resolved-FAFR Submitted or Resolved-CancelledThen the case will be resolved-cancelled and the PVR initial letter will not be sent

Name: PVR:  Ability to Edit PVR Post QC (S.20)
Acceptance Criteria: PARP will allow the ability to edit a case in statuses post Ready for QC (e.g., Results Pharm Contact, Ready for FAFR, Results Corr Fail, or Resolved FAFR submitted) to a manager or superuser (offshore and onshore) with an available edit button. The button can be found in the Actions drop down unless IT has a different solution.   Once the edit button is clicked, the case will move to a new status called Ready for QC Edit where only a Superuser or a Manager can edit.If the case was in pending consolidation, the edit button, once pressed, will take the case out of any pending consolidation.   if the case is pending email, fax or consolidation, once the edit button is clicked, PARP should prevent the correspondence from going on where possible (likely not possible with pending fax) and allow the user to edit the case.PARP will keep a record of the originally entered values by the reviewing auditor, all the QC values and the revised QC values.  The details of the original QC values will be stored and displayed in the audit trail of the case.   The revised QC data inputs will override the existing QC editable field inputs.Once the case is revised, PARP must allow the user to request, preview, and generate a revised PVR results letter to be sent to the pharmacy, using a new template called Revised PVR Results Letter.  This new template should only be used if a results letter was previously sent.  If the results letter was not sent yet, the system will use the original PVR Results letter template.Pega Team will provide the JSON fields for the Revised PVR Results letter.Once the letter is generated, the case will proceed to the pharmacy contact screen to send the letter and the case will proceed to the status of Results Pharm Contact. If the pharmacy is part of a consolidation group, it will follow the same schedule as other results letters to consolidate and send letters.  The status will be results pending consol.If the pharmacy is on the No PVR Results Letter BMT, the case will move to Ready for FAFR, unless the case had already been in FAFR Submitted previously. If the case status was in FAFR Submitted previously, once the letter is successfully sent, the case will move directly to FAFR Submitted and bypass the Ready for FAFR.If the letter fails to send, it will move to the Results Corr Failed queue.Once the Revised PVR Results letter is sent successfully, the status will change to Ready for FAFR, unless it was previously FAFR Submitted. When a FAFR is submitted and a FAFR report is generated containing a revised case, any “final” values for that case will be based upon the Revised fields (e.g., final validated quantity, final validated days supply, final discrepancy code, final discrepancy description, final discrepancy code 2, new final adjusted amount, final adjusted amount, audit comments, etc.)When a case is revised and submitted, a case note will be required before the submit is complete.If a results letter was previously sent, in the correspondence tab, once a Revised Results letter is sent, the original contact method, contact detail and fulfillment timestamps will be overridden with the revised results letter information.   The original results letter correspondence info (contact method, contact detail and fulfillment timestamps) will display in the audit trail of the case or in the case notes so that the user is aware of when and how the original correspondence was sent.  The audit trail of the case will indicate that the case was revised and will timestamp when it was moved to Ready for QC Edit and include the username.Once a case has been revised, the PVR details tab will indicate that the case has been revised with a field called “Revised”.  A “Y” next to the field will indicate that it has been revised.  All letters are in red font if PARP can accommodate.  The Revised field will only appear if the case was revised.20. Added 10/5/23: For cases that were originally No Response and skipped QC because user was on the Skip QC BMT, the option to edit QC should be available for those cases.21. Added 10/5/23:  For cases that were underwent QC edit, any fields that were updated should be counted towards the QC errors for auditors who initially worked the case; the QC report should also be updated to remove QC errors attributed to a user if there was truly no error after the edit is done.  If during QC edit, the fields are changed back to how the original reviewer had entered them, then no error should be attributed to the reviewer.22. Added 10/5/23:  If a manager/superuser originally performed the review in progress on the case, the same manager/superuser will not be able to do the QC edit for the same case.

If granting extension after reminder letter, then we don't need to send the letter Scenario #1: User grants an extension in the systemGiven a pharmacy requests an extension to the initial request for recordsWhen the user selects the option to grant extension to a case in the systemThen the system will update the original due date by adding 3 more business days  Scenario #2: Documenting the extension in the systemGiven a user chooses the grant extension option in the systemWhen the option is chosenThen the system will require the user to enter a reason for the extension (free text) and the system will capture the username and the date and time Scenario #3: System pushes due date outGiven the extension was grantedWhen the user selects the option to extend in the systemThen the system will allow for records to be received through the new due date Scenario #4: Initial Audit Records Received Request Response (within new due date)Given a pharmacy responds to the initial audit records request  PVR request for records within new due dateWhen a system successfully captures the inbound correspondenceThen the system indicates update the status to """"ready for review""""  ""Response Received"" Scenario #5: Initial Audit Records Request No Response (not within new due date)Given a pharmacy does not respond to the initial audit records PVR request for records within new due dateWhen the new due date has passed Then the system indicates   update the status to """"No Response to initial request""""  Interrelated User Stories:Audit Timeframe Due DateAudit Timeline-Pharmacy Responses to Initial Records RequestCase StatusWorklist Status

Name: PVR: Courtesy Reminder Letter (Email/Fax)

A response is required within by the due date of the original letter. If no response is received by the due date the Prescription Validation request will be processed as no response received. Please note if responding to this email with attachment(s), our file size limit is 14MB per attachment. We accept multiple emails or zip file(s) if needed. "" The due date in the reminder letter should be the same as the due date in the successfully sent original letter If the reminder letter fail the status will be updated to ""Reminder Corr Failed"" After the system confirms that the reminder letter has been sent successfully then the status will update to ""Final Waiting for Response"" and the date the letter was sent should be displayed in the correspondence tab of the Case Audit Details If granting extension before reminder letter, then we will send reminder letter with new due date. Name: PVR: Consolidate Emails for Same NCPDP
Acceptance Criteria: Acceptance Criteria: All PVR cases for the same NCPDP should be consolidated into one email The letter will have a barcode to tie it to the case in PARP,  all claims for the same NCPDP will be include on the Records Transmittal Page (see screenshot) If the consolidation group is present in the Pharmacy Contact BMT, then all of  the letters will be consolidated by chain code the specified consolidation group.  Consolidated letters would be emailed the same time according to the PVR status   Init PVR Request - 12 PM ET  Pending Consol - email as soon as the letters are ready   Reminder - 2PM ET  Pending Consol - email 10am PST  Result Pending Consol - email at 7PM ET 4pm PST   If an email has already been sent to a NCPDP or Chain on a given day, the system should not select additional claims for that NCPDP or Chain in the same day so as to avoid sending multiple emails in the same day While the letters are being consolidated the PVR status should be ""Init Pending Consol"" Once the consolidated emails have been successfully sent then the status will update to ""Init Waiting for Response"" When the PVR status is ""Ready for Reminder"", the system will consolidate all the reminder letters from the same NCPDP or chain pharmacies into one email.  While the letters are being consolidated, the status should be ""Reminder Pending Consol""  When the PVR status is ""Results Pharm Contact"", the system will consolidate all the result letters for the same NCPDP or chains (except for the chains who receive weekly PVR report) into one email.  Once the letters are being consolidated, the PVR status should be ""Result Pending Consol"" Once letters have been prepared by Inspire, there will be a 2-hour delay before consolidation occurs to allow the business to address any failed letter generations (so that consolidation can occur for those emails) and to spot check letters.    The Initial Letter Date in PVR Detail Tab will be update with the new date once the Init letter has been sent  Scenario #1: Consolidating claims for one NCPDPGiven ML has selected more than 1 claim for an NCPDP and they have been loaded into PARPWhen the claim is ready to be sent in the PVR notification letterThen the system will consolidate the claims for that NCPDPD into 1 letter Scenario #2: Include all claims for an NCPDP on the Records Transmittal PageGiven claims for an NCPDP have been consolidated into one letterWhen the letter is sentThen all claim numbers for that NCPDP will be include on the Records Transmittal Page Scenario #3: Batching emails by Consolidation GroupGiven letters have been consolidated by claims for the same NCPDPWhen those NCPDPDs are included in the consolidation group in the Pharmacy Contact BMTThen the system will consolidate the letters under a single email to the same consolidation group Scenario #4: Sending consolidated chain letters base on the PVR statusGiven letters for NCPDPs have been consolidate by consolidation groupWhen the PVRs are ready to be sentThen the system will send them base on their status Init Pending Consol - Email as soon as they are ready Reminder Pending Consol - Email at 10am PST (7am EST) Result Pending Consol - Email at 4pm PST (1pm EST) Scenario #5: Preventing multiple emails to a pharmacy in the same dayGiven a new claim needs to be selected for PVR in order to meet the 1300 claim per day goalWhen an email has already been sent to an NCPDP or chain on a given dayThen the system will not select another claim from that same NCPDP or chain in the given day (to avoid sending more than 1 fax per day to an NCPDP or chain) Scenario #6: Init Pending ConsolGiven the system is searching for the claims for the same NCPDP or chainWhen the letters are being consolidatedThen the status should change to ""Init Pending Consol"" Scenario #7: Init waiting for ResponseGiven the letters have been successfully sent to the pharmacyWhen the status is being updatedThen the status should change to ""Init Waiting for Response"" Scenario #8: Reminder Pending ConsolGiven the PVR status is ""Ready for Reminder""When the system is consolidating the same claims to send a reminder letter to the same NCPDP or chainThen the status should be ""Reminder Pending Consol"" Scenario #9: Results Pending Consol Given the PVR status is ""Result Pharm Contact""When the system is consolidating the same claims to send a result letter with finding to the same NCPDP or chain, except for the chain who receives weekly reportThen the status should be ""Result Pending Consol""

Name: PVR: No Response to Records Request
Acceptance Criteria: Acceptance Criteria: On the day after the due date for a given PVR, if records from the pharmacy have not been received then the status will update to ""No Response"" Auditors working the ""No Response"" Queue will be routed PVRs in ""No Response"" status when they hit the Get Next The No Response screen can mimic the DSK Prelim or Final No Response screens The user will need to confirm if a response has been received (Drop down ""No response received"" or ""Response received"" before they can proceed) If user indicates that documents were received the system will prompt them to attach the documents and to record the date the documents were received (both are required and user cannot proceed without completing both) Once user attaches the documents, then the audit will proceed to the next step and status will update to ""Response Received""  Scenario #1: No Response by Due DateGiven a request for records has been sent to a pharmacyWhen it is one day past the due dateThen the system will  update the case status to ""No Response"" Scenario #2: Working No Response queueGiven a case is in ""No Response"" statusWhen the case is opened in the No Response screenThen the system will ask the user to confirm that the pharmacy did not respond (response is required in order to proceed) Scenario #3: Documents received needed manual attachmentGiven documents were receivedWhen the user indicates that documents were receivedThen the system will prompt the user to attach the documents and record the date the documents were received before they can proceed Scenario #4: User manually attaches documentsGiven the user manually attaches the documents receivedWhen the documents are attached to the caseThen the case will move on to the next step and the status will be changed to ""Response Received""

Name: PVR: System Automatically Sends PVR Request Letter (Email/Fax only)
Acceptance Criteria: Acceptance Criteria: I need the system to generate the PVR Request Letter with the appropriate data fields completed (JSON). Case status will be ""Pending Letter Generation"" I need the system to access the Pharmacy Contact Preference BMT or Pharmacy Details to determine if the letter will be sent by email or by fax If the Consolidation Group in the Pharmacy Contact Preference BMT is blank then there is no need to consolidate the correspondence and should be sent as soon as the letter is ready If the pharmacy contact information is not found in the Pharmacy Contact Preference BMT, then PARP will reference the Pharmacy Details table and use the pharmacy fax number.  PARP will not use the email address found in the Pharmacy Details Table.   If the pharmacy contact information is not found in the Pharmacy Contact Preference BMT and a pharmacy fax number is not found in the Pharmacy Details table, then the PVR will be moved to Init Corr Failed If the pharmacy contact information is not found in either Pharmacy Contact Preference BMT or Pharmacy Details table then the PVR will move to the Init Corr Failed status If the fax or email fails, the status will update to Init Corr Failed after 3 attempts (attempts made every 15 10 mins) If the fax or email is successful, the status will update to Init Waiting for Response Once letters have been prepared by Inspire, there will be a 2-hour delay before email/fax is to go out, to allow the business to address any failed letter generations and to spot check letters.  Email will have the following:   Subject line:   Secure:  Optum Rx Notification - Action Required #  Body of Email:   Action Required - Please see attached for Optum Rx Notification. No Fax Number AvailableGiven a PVR Request Letter is being sent electronicallyWhen the pharmacy contact information is not found in the Pharmacy Contact Preference BMT and a pharmacy fax number is not found in the Pharmacy Details table, then the PVR will be moved to Init Corr FailedSo that a user can contact the pharmacy to verify the correct contact information. Scenario #6:  Init Corr FailedGiven the system search for pharmacy info in the Pharmacy Contact Preference BMT or Pharmacy Details TableWhen the pharmacy info is not found in either placeThen the case status will be ""Init Corr Failed"" Scenario #7: Fax/email failedGiven a fax or email PVR Request LetterWhen the letter fails to be sentThen the case status will update to ""Init Corr failed"" Scenario #8: Fax/email successfulGiven a fax or email PVR Request LetterWhen the letter was sent successfulThen the case status will update to ""Init Waiting for Response"" Scenario #9: 2-hour delayGiven a fax or email PVR Request LetterWhen the letter generation is successfulThen there will be a 2-hour delay before email/fax is to go out, to allow the business to address any failed letter generations and to spot check letters.   Scenario #10:   Email subject line/bodyGiven an email PVR request letterWhen the email is generatedThen the email will contain: Subject line:   Secure:  Optum Rx Notification - Action Required # Body of Email:   Action Required - Please see attached for Optum Rx Notification. Please note if responding to this email with attachment(s), our file size limit is 14MB per attachment. We accept multiple emails or zip file(s) if needed.Scenario #11:Given the PVR Request letterWhen it was successfully sentThen the Init Letter Date in PVR Detail Tab will be update with the sent date

Name: PVR:  Automated Job Failures (S.11)
Acceptance Criteria: If case creation fails, we need the system to alert the business as soon as possible and to have a back-up plan to create the cases ad hoc should the automated job fails If Init/Reminder letters are not generated, we need the system to alert the business as soon as possible and to allow the business to create letters (see US5440320) ad-hoc If all email job fails, we need the system to alert the business as soon as possible and retry again at least 3 times in the next 1 hour until resolved. If the email retry persists to fail after 1 hour, we need a bulk action that allows for all emails to be sent. If the fax job fails, we need the system to alert the business as soon as possible and retry again in the next 1 hour until resolved. If the fax retry fails after 1 hour, we need a bulk action that allows for all faxes to be sent. If any email consolidation fail (Init Pending Consol or Reminder Pending Consol), we need the system to alert the business as soon as possible and retry again in the next 1 hour until resolved If consolidation email retry fails after 1 hour, we need a bulk action that allows for consolidation of emails to be completed and emails to be sent according to the email consolidation rules. Notification will be send to PARP support team and the business (OptumRx_PVR_Leaders@Optum.com)

Name: PVR: System Tracks PVR Due Date
Acceptance Criteria: Acceptance Criteria When the PVR is initiated either by a user or by the system, the system captures the date that the PVR request letter is successfully sent (via fax or email). PVR initiation date visible in the PVR details The system tracks ""due in days"" for pharmacy response The due date logic is 7 business days, excluding weekends and holidays as stated on the Federal Holidays BMT, from date of PVR request. A PVR is considered overdue if there is no response by 11:59PM ET on the due date.   The JSON Dispute Timeframe for Inspire is set to 7. The due date is configurable by the business if needed and would apply to new PVR requests after the change is requested.  Scenario #1: PVR Initiation DateGiven a PVR is initiatedWhen the  PVR Request letter is successfully sent to the pharmacyThen the system captures the PVR “initiation date” and tracks business days until due Scenario #2: Initiation date is reportableGiven the PVR initiation dateWhen accessing PVR detailsThen the user can see the initiation date (displayed as Initial Letter Date) Scenario #4: ""Due in Days""Given a PVRWhen the system establishes the due of the PVRThen the system tracks ""due in days"" for pharmacy response Scenario #5:  Due Date LogicGiven a PVRWhen a PVR Request is initiatedThen the system will use the following logic:  The due date logic is 7 business days, excluding weekends and holidays as stated on the Federal Holidays BMT, from date of PVR request Scenario #6:  Overdue TimeframeGiven a PVRWhen PVR responses are not receivedThen the system will use 11:59PM ET on the due date as the time in which documents must be marked as received.  If not received by this time, the PVR is considered overdue and the status will become No Response. Scenario #7:  Dispute TimeframeGiven a PVR letterWhen Inspire creates the Request and Reminder letterThen the letters will contain the due date (7 business days) which is the JSON: DisputeTimeframe

PVR: Preventing PVR Initiation of Same Rx Number+NCPDP With Other Flows
Acceptance Criteria: Before a PVR case is initiated, PARP will do a check against the other flows and remove any claims from a PVR case that have the same Rx number at the same NCPDP ID that is present in the OA/DA correspondence table.If the PVR case has more than 1 claim, only the claim that has an Rx number+NCPDPID duplicated with another flow will be removed.  The remaining claim(s) will continue to be included in the PVR case initiation.If the PVR case has only 1 claim and the claim has an Rx number+NCPDPID that is duplicated with another flow, the case will be resolved-cancelled and a PVR initial letter will not be sent. Given before PVR case is initiatedWhen PARP will cross-check the claim(s) in the PVR case to see if any claim has the same Rx number from the same NCPDP ID as a claim that is in the OA/DA correspondence table and the OA/DA is in a status other than Resolved-FAFR Submitted or Resolved-CancelledThen PARP will remove the claim(s) with the duplicated Rx number(s) from the PVR case Given a PVR case has more than 1 claimWhen one or more claim(s) has/have an Rx number+NCPDPID duplicated with another flow in OA/DA correspondence table and the OA/DA is in a status  other than Resolved-FAFR Submitted or Resolved-CancelledThen the duplicated claim(s) will be removed from the case and any remaining claims will continue to be included in the PVR during case initiation Given a PVR case has only 1 claimWhen the claim has an Rx number+NCPDPID duplicated with another flow in OA/DA correspondence table and the OA/DA is in a status other than Resolved-FAFR Submitted or Resolved-CancelledThen the case will be resolved-cancelled and the PVR initial letter will not be sent
